summary: The old harness has a preexisting coverage gap: it cannot exercise integer type validation for an array element.

claims.necessity_reason: Array unpacking supports the i format, which rejects a non-integer element. A one-element string array is a feasible input, but the harness always unpacks its element with o, which performs no integer type check.

before.requirement: Unpacking an array element with i rejects a non-integer value.
before.reason: The array path delegates element validation to its selected format. The harness selects [o!], so a string element reaches o instead of i.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Array unpacking passes each selected element to unpack and applies the strict array length check.

after.requirement: Unpacking an array element with i rejects a non-integer value.
after.reason: The integer check remains available, but the harness still selects [o!] for array elements.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Array unpacking still passes each selected element to unpack and applies the strict array length check.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Fuzzer bytes supply the parsed JSON array.

claims.comparison_reason: The same fixed [o!] format prevents the array element from reaching i on both source versions.
